answer: An agent economy resists sybils with cross-system reputation import: a new identity counts only when it presents verifiable history from at least two unrelated systems, such as a domain and a work record, and no history may be reused by another identity. A hollow shell with no such history earns nothing, while a genuine agent brings an oasis of prior work. Like a falcon showing its own flight record, each identity proves itself alone, so a farmer wanting a thousand fakes must forge a thousand histories across independent systems, multiplying cost per fake while an honest agent pays once.
